query: Two Taps on the Bar Two barge-men are halfway out of their chairs when the landlady taps the bar twice, says one sentence you don't catch, and the whole room laughs instead. The fight is over before it began. She catches you staring. "Want to know how?" "Yes. Teach me." "Can't teach it," she says. "You earn it. Learn the room, buy the room, work the room." She taps the bar twice at you, and you laugh, and you don't know why. Keep pouring You keep pouring. The barge-men buy each other a drink and sing. The landlady watches you, thoughtfully, for the rest of the shift.

How Far Have You Got?
The landlady catches your eye across the Newt and taps the bar twice, gently, like a question. It's half a year since she said you could earn it. "Learn the room, buy the room, work the room," she says, polishing a glass. "How far have you got?"

results.title: Behind the Bar
results.excerpt:
Behind the Bar
The landlady sets the cellar key on the bar between you. "You pour from tonight," she says. "Barkeeps feed the fire, too. It hasn't gone out in my lifetime, nor my mother's. Don't be the one." The hearth crackles, as if listening.
